archetype.name: Dual-Threat (efficiency-first passer)
archetype.definition: A rushing threat who runs a low-volume, run-leaning offense and does real damage as a passer, getting big yards per attempt from accurate short and intermediate throws while his legs bail out broken plays.

report.headline: Four games of league-best efficiency against soft defenses, now an ankle question.
report.take:
Jackson's 2026 so far is four games and 96 attempts, and in that window he has been the most efficient passer in the league. His 10.74 adjusted net yards per dropback ranks 1st of 45, his CPOE of 8.29 ranks 1st, and his 0.363 EPA per dropback ranks 3rd. He has done it in a Ravens offense that passes less than situations call for (-3 pass rate over expected, 21st), so the counting stats look ordinary: 241.8 yards a game ranks 17th and 1.5 touchdowns a game ranks 17th. His 9.3 passing EPA per game ranks 5th, which is closer to the truth. He doesn't throw much, but almost every throw is worth something.

Two things drive it. The first is the middle of the field. Throws of 10-19 air yards produce 0.904 EPA, short throws 0.504 with all five of his short touchdowns, and the middle of the field 0.688. The second is Zay Flowers: 19 targets at 1.46 EPA each. The legs are back too. After a down 2025 on the ground (26.8 rushing yards a game, 12th in rushing yards), he is at 36 a game, 4th among QBs. His 10 scrambles have produced 6 first downs at 0.48 EPA each. He has also cut his pressure-to-sack rate to 29.2% from last year's 43.9%, which ranked 51st of 62.

The numbers flatter him in a few places. Every opponent he has faced now ranks 21st or worse in defensive EPA, including Dallas at 30th. The CPOE is far above anything in his career; his previous best was 4.55 in 2024. It also sits beside a 16.7% bad-throw rate that ranks 32nd of 38, a trait that has followed him for years. That gap says some of the completion luck will fade. The situational football has been thin as well. On third down his EPA is 0.01 with a 34.8% conversion rate, partly because he faces an average of 9.2 yards to go. In the red zone his EPA is -0.07 and his CPOE -7, even with four touchdowns there.

He sprained his ankle in Week 4, playing only 52% of the snaps, and Tyler Huntley started Weeks 5-7. The site lists him Out, but he was limited in practice and Jesse Minter says he is in a decent spot to play at Buffalo. If he returns, the efficiency should settle somewhere below these league-leading marks but still in the top tier. That is where he lived in 2019 and 2024, when his EPA per play ranked 2nd and 3rd. The volume ceiling stays capped by how run-heavy the offense is. The ankle also puts the designed runs and scrambles at risk in his first game back, and those are much of his edge.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field efficiency at volume-light rates
strengths.body: His intermediate throws (0.904 EPA on 15 attempts) and middle-of-the-field throws (0.688) are where the yards per attempt come from. He is still pushing the ball past the sticks on average, not padding stats with checkdowns. The 15-attempt intermediate sample will cool. His top-tier yards per attempt did hold up in 2024 and 2025, though, so the overall shape is real.

strengths.title: Zay Flowers connection carries the passing game
strengths.body: Flowers has turned 19 targets into 27.7 EPA, the bulk of the passing value, while Mark Andrews draws more targets at a much lower return. That per-target rate is unsustainable on any sample. Still, it shows a quarterback and a top receiver who are hitting in rhythm, and that matters against a defense that leaks to WR1s.

strengths.title: Legs back, and the sacks down
strengths.body: Rushing is back to 36 yards a game, 4th among QBs, after last year's dip. Scrambles have been efficient and moved the chains. The extended plays are no longer costing him as many sacks: his pressure-to-sack rate is down sharply from last year's bottom-tier mark. The 2024 version of him did the same thing, so this looks like a return to form rather than a fluke, provided the ankle allows it.

concerns.title: Accuracy numbers ahead of the tape
concerns.body: A CPOE of 8.29 is a career outlier: up 6.5 points on last year and well above his 2024 peak. Meanwhile his bad-throw rate ranks 32nd of 38, and in 2025 it ranked 43rd of 63. Add four opponents who all rank 21st or worse defensively, and some of that completion percentage is soft coverage and short-sample luck. Expect it to come back toward the low-to-mid single digits.

concerns.title: Third down and red zone lag
concerns.body: The money downs haven't matched the rest. His third-down EPA is essentially zero with a 34.8% conversion rate, though an average of 9.2 yards to go shows early-down stalls set those up. Red-zone EPA and CPOE are both negative despite four touchdowns there. On 23 and 15 plays these are hints rather than verdicts, but they are the reason the scoreboard hasn't always followed the efficiency, as in the 17-24 loss to New Orleans.

concerns.title: Ankle plus a run-first ceiling
concerns.body: He hasn't played since Week 4, when he logged 52% of the snaps, and the ankle sprain threatens exactly the scrambles and designed runs that separate him from other passers. Even fully healthy, at 24 attempts a game in a below-average pass-rate offense, his passing volume depends on game script.

trend.note: Three of his four games produced passing EPA between 10.3 and 11.9, with a 3.3 dud against New Orleans the exception. His last-three rates sit almost exactly on his season marks. The open question is the ankle and three missed starts, not form.

nextGame.headline: If the ankle holds, Buffalo's defense is the softest yet
nextGame.body:
Buffalo ranks last in defensive EPA and 29th against the pass. It allows 314.2 yards a game to quarterbacks (31st) and the 28th-worst explosive pass rate, and it gets home with the 26th-ranked sack rate. That is a worse unit than any of the four he carved up. It also hurts WR1s most of all, at 9.8 PPR points over their averages, last in the league, which points straight at Flowers. The Bills offense ranks 1st in EPA, Baltimore is a 3.5-point underdog, and the total is 53.5. That script should push the Ravens off their run-leaning tendencies and give him more dropbacks than usual.

Availability is the whole story. Jackson is listed Out but practiced in a limited fashion, and the coach is optimistic. If he plays, watch whether he runs freely; a cautious, pocket-bound version gives up his scramble value. Guard Olaivavega Ioane (89% of snaps) is questionable with a knee injury after leaving the Bengals game, a hit to interior protection if he sits. On Buffalo's side, safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (89% of snaps) is suspended, thinning a secondary that already struggles. DT Ed Oliver is questionable, and so is WR DJ Moore, whose status shapes how hard Buffalo pushes the pace.

keyMatchups.title: Flowers against a WR1 sieve
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo has let lead receivers beat their own averages by more than any other defense and allows 0.52 EPA per WR1 target, 26th. With Gardner-Johnson suspended, the back end loses its most-used safety. Flowers' 1.46 EPA per target won't hold, but this is the spot for it to stay hot.

keyMatchups.title: A weak pass rush meets his pocket
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's 4.2% sack rate ranks 26th. That gives Jackson time to hold the ball, as his 3.11-second time to throw shows he likes to, and to find the intermediate windows where he has done his best work. An Ioane absence is the one thing that could tilt the interior.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script lifts his volume
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's league-best offense against a Ravens defense ranked 20th, with the Ravens as underdogs, suggests Baltimore will have to throw more than its usual run-first rate. More dropbacks against a 29th-ranked pass defense is the formula for a ceiling game.

nextGame.watch: Whether he scrambles and keeps on designed runs early. A mobile Jackson against this defense is a ceiling game; a protected ankle makes him a very good pocket passer with a capped total.

restOfSeason.body:
Assuming he is back, expect elite-but-not-historic efficiency: yards per attempt and ANY/A near the top of the league, with CPOE drifting down toward his 2024 level rather than staying above 8. The rushing should settle near this year's rate once the ankle is fully right, and the lower pressure-to-sack rate looks more like his 2024 self than a fluke. Volume is the limiter. In an offense that leans on the run, figure roughly 215-265 passing yards and 1.3-2.0 passing touchdowns a game, with more in shootouts like Buffalo and less in games the Ravens control. When they lead comfortably, his efficiency has gone negative and the offense shuts down.

The softness of the early schedule matters. All four opponents rank in the bottom half defensively, so his raw efficiency will likely dip against better units even as his true level stays high. The red-zone and third-down numbers should improve toward average on more plays. Some of his touchdown production comes from short throws that won't keep converting at this rate.
swingFactors: How mobile the ankle lets him be
Whether Flowers keeps producing at a lead-receiver level
Game scripts forcing the Ravens to throw more

confidence.note: Only 96 attempts, all against weak defenses, then an ankle sprain and three missed starts.
